page: The Amazon Web Services c4.xlarge is a fourth-generation compute-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It runs on a 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System cache is configured with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 25 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 8.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote network storage volumes and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results reflect the aging architecture of the Haswell-generation processor. In single-core testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 1480.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1149.0, placing it within average to weak performance tiers. Multi-threaded processing scores 3903.16 in stress-ng and 2516.0 in Geekbench, constrained by the dual-core physical topology. Memory throughput measures 25.92 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 22.39 GB/sec for writes, with PassMark memory scoring in the bottom decile at 1088.78. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, FMA, and AES, supporting moderate throughput in standard tasks like gzip compression at 24.42 GB/sec and small-model LLM generation at 81.87 tokens per second.

Given its older hardware generation, the c4.xlarge is generally suitable for legacy workloads, light batch processing, front-end web serving, and secondary compute tasks that do not saturate high memory bandwidth or require modern vector extensions like AVX-512.
